passage.title: 'How Stories Survive', a teacher-written article for TGA
paras: Long before printing, whole communities kept their knowledge in memory. Muslims preserved the Qur'an both by heart and in writing: many companions memorised it, and it was gathered into a single written copy, then copied and sent to the great cities. Today archives record the voices of elderly people before their memories are lost. The lesson is the same in every age: a story survives only if someone decides it is worth carrying.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'Compare how the article and the poem present keeping stories alive.' Starter: 'Both texts suggest...'

questions.q: Extend: explain why oral testimony is valuable to historians
questions.a: It records experiences that no official document captured, like the poem's personal voice.
